leading_positions.synthesis: Six of the eight members prefer the optical lattice clock as the sole prize part, with Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye as laureates. All six rely on the same core case: the magic-wavelength lattice as a single well-defined invention, uncertainties near 1e-18 reproduced in many laboratories, and consequences for the SI second, relativistic geodesy and tests of constants. Citations differ only slightly: kroll-stefan, lindroth-eva and mehlig-bernhard add a 1e-18-level clause, and the others use the bare invention-and-development wording. Not shared is any agreement on how much the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes weigh, whether the two-name credit is complete, or whether to wait for the redefinition of the second. Two further members, eriksson-olle and olsson-eva, list B048 as an alternative rather than their preferred configuration, and several members' statements say all eight ranked B048 in their opening top three.

Only eriksson-olle prefers topological insulators with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, citing a Z2 prediction confirmed by experiment in HgTe and nearly two decades of independent confirmation. The case pairs theory with experiment, but it omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the early three-dimensional work, and it overlaps in subject with the 2016 topology prize. B019 is an alternative for danielsson-ulf, johansson-goran, kroll-stefan, lindroth-eva, mehlig-bernhard and olsson-eva, which is support as a fallback and not as a preferred configuration.

Only olsson-eva prefers spherical-aberration correction in TEM with Rose, Haider and Urban, as a concrete invention that removed a limit recognised since Scherzer and now underpins atomic-resolution imaging. She states that no one else ranked it in the top three, that it follows the 1986 microscopy prize, that Krivanek and STEM correction work is omitted, and that she would regard B048 as a defensible outcome. Her alternatives are B048 and B019.

areas_of_agreement: Six of eight members prefer B048 (Katori and Ye) as their sole prize part, and eriksson-olle and olsson-eva name it as an alternative, so B048 appears in all eight files as either preferred or alternative.

Members agree on the scientific content of the lattice-clock case: the magic-wavelength condition removing the trapping light shift, many-atom interrogation, uncertainties near 1e-18, and independent reproduction across laboratories.
Members who discuss B048 name the same downstream consequences: the pending SI redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy, and constraints on varying constants and dark-sector couplings.

Members who prefer B048 treat its two-name attribution (Katori for the concept and first strontium realisation, Ye for record accuracy and many-body regimes) as cleaner than the other shortlisted entries discussed, though several state that this rests on recollection or general knowledge.

The same three reservations about B048 recur in every supporter's statement: overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, credit to other lattice-clock groups, and the unfinished redefinition of the second.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a distinct invention or an extension of the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes; kroll-stefan and danielsson-ulf argue in their exchange that it is a different concept (many atoms cancelling the trapping Stark shift), while all B048 supporters list the overlap as their main reservation.

Whether instrument-enabling or measurement-capability work (B048, B028) ranks as fundamental discovery against concept-level work such as topological insulators (B019); eriksson-olle and olsson-eva each press a different version of this comparison.
Whether a further topology-related award is warranted after the 2016 prize (eriksson-olle's uncertainty on B019).

Whether the Higgs discovery (B054) is defensible as a lead; the chair's file calls it the most consequential outstanding experimental result in particle physics, while danielsson-ulf objects that the three-person limit makes any ATLAS and CMS trio arbitrary.
attribution_disputes: B048: whether Katori and Ye alone fairly cover the field, given Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Bloom and the Paris and PTB groups outside the supplied names, and where the boundary with Hall and Haensch (2005) lies.
B019: whether Kane, Mele and Molenkamp can be honoured without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who proposed the HgTe route, and without Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, and the Bi2Se3 experimenters.
B028: whether a TEM-only trio of Rose, Haider and Urban implicitly settles a priority question against Krivanek and the STEM aberration-correction work.
B054 and B033 (the chair's alternatives): any three of Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee omit others with equal claims, and Halzen and Karle may not capture AMANDA and Baikal precursors.
Several members (johansson-goran, olsson-eva, kroll-stefan, pearce-mark) say their priority and weighting judgments rest on recollection or general knowledge rather than verified records.
maturity_disputes: Whether to wait for the formal redefinition of the second before recognising the lattice clock; lindroth-eva judges the demonstrated impact already outweighs the timing argument, while danielsson-ulf, johansson-goran, kroll-stefan, mehlig-bernhard and pearce-mark list it as an open uncertainty.

Whether the technological payoff of topological insulators is still largely prospective (eriksson-olle's own caveat on dissipationless edge channels and Majorana platforms) given nearly two decades of independent confirmation.
Whether IceCube (B033) is slightly less mature than the clock because individual source identification is still thin (danielsson-ulf and pearce-mark).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: johansson-goran: possible recusal issue for B001 (circuit QED) as a circuit and waveguide QED theorist and director of WACQT at Chalmers; no connection apparent to Katori or Ye.

kroll-stefan: time in John Hall's laboratory (2005 laureate whose comb work underlies lattice clocks), noted as a field proximity and possible indirect link to the precision-spectroscopy community; proximity to B003 and B002 through rare-earth-ion quantum memories, Lund colleagues, WACQT and Deep Light Vision; no decisive conflict with Katori or Ye.

olsson-eva: works in transmission electron microscopy and leads the international microscopy federation, so may know Rose, Haider or Urban professionally; would recuse from B028 if the committee deems it a conflict.

pearce-mark (chair): membership in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur and an accelerator-based particle-physics doctorate bear on B033 and B054, flagged for a recusal discussion if either becomes the lead; none apparent for B048.
danielsson-ulf, eriksson-olle, lindroth-eva and mehlig-bernhard report no specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee word a B048 citation that covers the lattice clock as an invention without trespassing on the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes, and does it regard the overlap as a real obstacle?
Is a two-name Katori and Ye credit acceptable given Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Bloom and the Paris and PTB groups, and which priority details can be verified rather than recalled?
Should the committee act now on B048 or wait for the redefinition of the second, and what in the record would change any member's view?

Should a second prize part accompany B048 (kroll-stefan raises B003 trapped-ion quantum logic as a possibility, mehlig-bernhard sees no natural fit for a three-laureate split), or is a single-achievement, two-laureate prize preferable?
For B019, can the citation honour the Z2 prediction and the HgTe observation without crediting Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and how much does the 2016 topology prize weigh against it?
For B028, how should the committee treat Krivanek and STEM aberration correction, and is a second instrumentation prize after the 1986 microscopy prize acceptable?
Do the chair's connections to B033 and B054, and the flags from kroll-stefan, johansson-goran and olsson-eva, require any recusal handling in round 2?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a strong convergence on B048 (Katori and Ye): six members, including the chair, prefer it as their sole prize part, and two more list it as an alternative. The other preferred configurations, B019 from eriksson-olle and B028 from olsson-eva, are each held by one member and carry specific attribution objections. The open issues are overlap with earlier prizes, completeness of credit, and timing relative to the redefinition of the second, and the B048 supporters raise these themselves. This summary counts only explicit positions in the eight files and is not a ruling.
